subject: Kickoff: Evaluation Charter & MAP for CardioFlow POC
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@cardioflow.ai>, Ravi Sinha <ravi.s@cardioflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: Evaluation Charter & MAP for CardioFlow POC

Hi Olivia / Ravi —

Thanks again for taking the time last week. Per our call, I wanted to kick off a short mutual action plan (MAP) to align on success criteria, evaluation benchmarks, and owners so we can hit the target decision date on May 21. Attached is a first-draft MAP and a starter benchmark suite (CSV) you'll see referenced below.

High-level goals (suggested):
- Technical: <10% false-positive rate on arrhythmia detection across the provided clinical dataset at 30s snippets.
- Latency: 95th percentile inference < 220ms on 2k token prompts for the live inference path.
- Cost: Target per-hour token cost <= our committed demo quota (we can iterate on batching settings).
- Business: Successful integration of Redwood API into demo UI and an internal stakeholder demo scheduled by 05/18.

Proposed owners (please confirm or nominate alternates):
- Success lead (timeline, stakeholder coordination): Jordan Blake (me)
- Technical lead (benchmarks, prompt library, eval harness): Marissa Cole
- Integration/Dev contact (sample dataset, API calls): Ravi Sinha (CardioFlow)
- Evaluation analyst (metric computations, dashboarding): Dylan Brooks

Immediate asks for this week:
1) Olivia/Ravi: Confirm dataset access scope and a point-of-contact for SFTP transfer (we need a de-identified sample of ~500 patient snippets).
2) CardioFlow: Review attached MAP and benchmark CSV; flag any missing business metrics.
3) Marissa/Dylan: Prepare an initial prompt set (10 prompts) focusing on edge cases (noisy telemetry, unusual rhythms) by EOD 4/27.

Timeline (draft):
- 4/25: Kickoff + MAP review (this email)
- 4/27: Initial prompt set + dataset access confirmed
- 5/6: First benchmark run + results review
- 5/12: Stakeholder demo (internal to CardioFlow)
- 5/18-5/21: Decision window / contract review

Attachments: CF_MAP_v1.docx (MAP draft), benchmark_suite_v1.csv (example metrics + test cases), roles_and_owners.xlsx (owner roster)

If that looks good I'll lock the MAP and we can track tasks in the shared Drive + HubSpot deal noted below.

Thanks — looking forward to working together.

—
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Olivia Grant <olivia@cardioflow.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ravi Sinha <ravi.s@cardioflow.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Evaluation Charter & MAP for CardioFlow POC

Thanks Jordan — this looks great and aligned with what we discussed.

Quick answers:
- Dataset: We can provision a de-identified SFTP drop by 4/27; I will loop in our data ops lead (CC'd: Ravi).
- Success criteria: The technical metrics look right; can we add a business metric — reduction in triage time for cardiology team (minutes saved) as a high-level KPI?

I'll review the MAP doc and give feedback by EOD 4/26. Ravi, can you confirm the SFTP details and preferred file format (CSV vs TFRecord)?

Best,
Olivia
Head of Product, CardioFlow
olivia@cardioflow.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Grant <olivia@cardioflow.ai>, Ravi Sinha <ravi.s@cardioflow.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Evaluation Charter & MAP for CardioFlow POC

Appreciate the clear breakdown, Jordan. I can own the prompt set and initial benchmark runs. Dylan — I think you should own the metric calculations and dashboard to speed reviews. Plan:
- Marissa: deliver prompt pack (10) + prompt tagging (edge case, noise, clinical label) by 4/27 EOD
- Dylan: scaffold evaluation notebook and metric definitions by 4/29; will use the attached CSV schema as a starting point.

Olivia — we prefer CSV (simple) for the first handoff; TFRecord only if you have an existing pipeline that relies on it. If SFTP is not convenient, we can accept a secure Drive link.

I'll also add a short section to the MAP with acceptance gates (pass/fail thresholds) and propose a canary test with 50 live inference calls before the demo.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@cardioflow.ai>, Ravi Sinha <ravi.s@cardioflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Evaluation Charter & MAP for CardioFlow POC

Thanks all — great rapid alignment.

Olivia: adding the triage-time KPI is a good call; I've updated the MAP (attached v1.1) to call that out as a secondary business metric.

Next actions I will own:
- Lock MAP v1.1 and post to Drive by 4/26 12:00pm PT
- Create HubSpot tasks for dataset transfer and prompt handoff
- Schedule the 5/6 benchmark review (30m) — proposing 10:00am PT; I'll send a calendar invite after you confirm availability

If there are no objections I'll mark Marissa as technical lead and Dylan as evaluation analyst in the MAP. Olivia/Ravi please confirm the SFTP or Drive preference and we'll go from there.

Cheers,
Jordan
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: CF_MAP_v1.1.docx (updated MAP), benchmark_suite_v1.csv, roles_and_owners.xlsx
